# Results — Study 411 (Ascending Triangle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **an ascending
triangle (flat resistance + rising lows) breaks upward and runs** — tested with the closest
**mechanical** definition of the figure on daily OHLC: a band of swing highs at a flat level, a
rising line through the intervening swing lows, and a confirmed close above the resistance, across
**SPY + 29 US large-caps**. We measure the forward return after each confirmed breakout as an
**excess over each name's own base rate** (does the figure beat buy-and-hold for that name?), with
a one-sample/HAC *t*, a **same-tape label-shuffle placebo**, a **down-break symmetry** myth-check,
and a synthetic positive control. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

> **Chart figures are partly subjective.** The ascending triangle is in the eye of the beholder.
> We do **not** claim to capture every triangle a human would draw — we test one transparent,
> reproducible mechanical definition and say so. A different rule set would find a different
> (overlapping) event set; the qualitative verdict is what travels.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted** (split + dividend) OHLC — 30 long-listed US large-caps incl. SPY (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-05-31** (last full bar **2026-05-29**; no partial month) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**21.4** years; 5,385 daily bars) |
| Fingerprint | `b660382b8af3` (sha1[:12] of the close panel) |
| Detector | flat resistance (≥3 swing highs within 4%) + rising-low trendline (positive slope, last low ≥5% above first) + first close clearing the rim |
| Events | **385** confirmed ascending-triangle **up**-breaks (SPY alone: **11**); **372** down-breaks (myth check) |
| Timing / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the breakout (no look-ahead); hold 5/10/20/40 days; **5 bps** one-way × 2 = 10 bps round trip |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026. A
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms that delisted after a failed breakout, which
> tilts post-breakout forward returns mildly **up** — i.e. the bias works *for* the figure, and it
> still doesn't certify. Total-return adjusted closes (we label them as such).

## The signal — forward return after a confirmed up-break, EXCESS over the base rate

The excess subtracts each name's own unconditional mean forward return, so the test is **"does the
figure beat buy-and-hold for that name?"** — not "is the market up." The **placebo p** is the share
of 5,000 draws of *random entry dates on the same tape* (same count) whose excess **beats** the
observed one — the honest control for the tape's own up-drift.

| horizon | n events | excess mean | raw mean | win-rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 385 | +0.10% | +0.39% | 51% | +0.56 | +0.60 | 0.46 | −0.00% |
| 10-day | 384 | +0.97% | +1.54% | 64% | **+3.85** | **+3.89** | 0.22 | +0.87% |
| 20-day | 384 | +1.47% | +2.60% | 65% | **+3.81** | **+4.05** | 0.21 | +1.37% |
| 40-day | 382 | +1.98% | +4.21% | 64% | **+3.78** | **+3.82** | 0.21 | +1.88% |

Read it carefully — this is the whole study. The **naive** one-sample/HAC *t* clears the desk's
**t ≥ 2** bar comfortably at 10/20/40 days (*t* ≈ 3.8–4.1), even on the *excess* over base rate.
Taken alone, that reads `REAL`. But the same-tape **placebo p stays ~0.21**: a random set of entry
dates on the same drifting names beats the breakout about **one time in five**. The *t*-against-zero
is fooled because the breakout *selects post-run-up dates*, and recently-rising names keep rising a
bit (momentum) — the placebo inherits that drift, the naive *t* does not. The number is real; its
**attribution to the triangle** is what's in doubt.

## Costs — they barely matter, because there's no placebo-clean edge to tax

A round trip is **5 bps one-way × 2 = 10 bps**. Net columns above. There is nothing to erode: the
gross excess is already inside the placebo cloud, so costs are a footnote, not the killer.

## Myth check — does it break UP far more than DOWN? (the symmetry test)

The cleanest within-study control. Run the **identical** detector but require a break *below* the
rising floor (the "bearish" resolution). If the figure genuinely chooses an upward direction, the
down-break excess should be **negative**, well under the up-break.

| horizon | n | down-break excess | raw | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 372 | −0.18% | +0.11% | −1.00 | 0.58 |
| 10-day | 370 | +0.37% | +0.95% | +1.15 | 0.39 |
| 20-day | 370 | +1.20% | +2.35% | +2.62 | 0.26 |
| 40-day | 369 | +2.16% | +4.42% | +3.39 | 0.20 |

The down-break — the resolution a chartist would call **bearish** — *also* drifts **up** at 20–40
days (+1.20% / +2.16%, *t* = 2.62 / 3.39), nearly matching the up-break. A figure that truly
*chose* a direction could not have its two resolutions drift the same way. The post-figure return
is a property of the **names** (momentum into resistance), not the **break direction**. "It breaks
upward" is the part that's busted.

## Robustness — strictness moves the *t*, not the placebo

| flat tol / min rise | n events | excess (20d) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3% / ≥7% (strict) | 234 | +1.07% | +2.12 | 0.32 |
| **4% / ≥5% (headline)** | **384** | **+1.47%** | **+3.81** | **0.21** |
| 6% / ≥4% (loose) | 513 | +1.57% | +4.63 | 0.16 |

The naive *t* swings with the sample (more events on a drifting tape → higher *t*), but the
**placebo p stays ~0.16–0.32 everywhere** — no setting pulls it under the 5% bar. That invariance
is the signature of a tape artefact: you can tune the *t*, you can't tune away the fact that random
dates do as well.

## Myth check — does it beat SPY buy-and-hold? (the README hook)

The hook asks specifically about **SPY**. The detector finds only **11** clean ascending triangles
on the SPY tape in 21 years — far too few to certify anything:

| horizon | n | excess vs SPY hold | raw | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 11 | +0.54% | +0.78% | +0.61 | 0.22 |
| 10-day | 11 | +1.03% | +1.50% | +0.84 | 0.14 |
| 20-day | 11 | +1.53% | +2.47% | +1.30 | 0.11 |
| 40-day | 11 | +1.69% | +3.54% | +1.03 | 0.18 |

With *n* = 11 and *t* ≈ 1 the SPY-only version is uncertifiable, and the broad-basket symmetry test
already showed the breakout direction is uninformative. The figure does **not** demonstrably beat
SPY buy-and-hold.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful (and the placebo is the right arbiter)

On a deterministic panel where we **plant** clean ascending triangles and a *known* post-breakout
drift, the detector + inference behave exactly as they must — and crucially, the **naive *t* can be
fooled by the planted geometry while the placebo is not**:

| planted edge | planted | detected | n | excess (20d) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 160 | 178 | 177 | +1.96% | +4.51 | 0.12 | 68% |
| **+0.20** (large planted drift) | 160 | 199 | 199 | +7.49% | **+13.98** | **0.000** | 83% |

With **no** planted continuation the naive *t* still reaches **4.51** — because the planted shape,
like a real triangle, selects post-run-up dates — but the **placebo holds at p = 0.12** (not
significant). Plant a real +20% continuation and everything explodes (*t* = 13.98, placebo
*p* = 0.000, win 83%). The engine *can* bank a true edge; the real tape simply doesn't have one
once the placebo speaks. This is precisely why we trust the placebo over the *t*.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The up-break excess-over-base-rate clears a naive bar (**+1.47% at 20 days,
  one-sample t = 3.81, HAC t = 4.05**), but the same-tape **placebo p = 0.21** (luck wins ~1-in-5),
  the strictness sweep keeps *p* at ~0.16–0.32, and a **zero-edge synthetic control reproduces
  t = 4.51 at placebo p = 0.12**. The number is real; its attribution to the figure is not. **WEAK,
  not REAL** — the *t* clears 2 only against a drifting-tape null the placebo corrects. Survivorship
  tilts the test *for* the figure and it still fails.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** What you'd be "trading" is the names' own up-drift / momentum into
  resistance — exactly what random dates capture. The SPY-only version rests on **11** events at
  *t* ≈ 1; costs are a footnote because there's no placebo-clean edge to tax. Nothing to deploy.
- **"Breaks up specifically"? — BUSTED.** The pattern's entire premise is *direction*, and the
  direction carries **no** information: the **down**-break of the identical figure also drifts up
  (+1.20% / +2.16% at 20/40 days, *t* = 2.62 / 3.39). Break up or break down, the stock drifts up
  the same. The triangle is a momentum tell dressed as a directional breakout signal.
